nodes.title: Integral section model
nodes.statement: Given a reduced proper rigid X over an algebraically closed complete K, a line bundle L and a finite affinoid cover U_i=Spa(R_i,R_i°) with affinoid intersections, choose sections s_j^(i). Require s_i^(i) to frame L, all ratios s_j^(i)/s_i^(i) to be power bounded, U_ij to be the unit locus of s_j^(i)/s_i^(i), and overlap differences divided by a frame to have norm at most |ϖ|. Transport the general formal gluing construction to these actual rings: 𝔛 has charts Spf R_i°, its generic fibre is X, and 𝔏 has integral frame s_i^(i). The sections reduce to global s̄_j modulo ϖ. The charts are D(s̄_i); 𝔛 is projective and 𝔏 ample. The structure sheaf on each chart is the power-bounded ring, with ϖ-completed localization on intersections.
hypotheses: 0≠ϖ∈𝔪_K; integral rings are R_i° rather than arbitrary plus rings.
On U_ik the overlap congruence is measured using s_i^(i); finite cover and reducedness are essential.
proofSteps: For J⊂J′ localize at the product of ratios indexed by J′\J, then complete; invoke formal gluing and its generic-fibre comparison.
Glue frame transition units; the overlap congruences glue the reduced sections.
The distinguished affine cover by reduced sections gives ampleness; apply the supplier projectivity criterion over O_K.

The canonical support morphism identifies (j!O⁺_X∞/p^m)^a with (I⁺_∞/p^m)^a on the étale site and its topological comparison site. The maps are natural in m and for the actual boundary-preserving level correspondences.

nodes.title: Boundary trace transport
nodes.statement: For normal integral finite-level chart rings R⊂S in a finite generically étale cover, with f a nonzerodivisor and S[f⁻¹] finite étale over R[f⁻¹], the algebra trace sends S to R. If J is the integral closure in S of an integrally closed ideal I⊂R, it sends J into I. Apply this to the actual boundary ideals in the anticanonical tower, then use its normalized Tate traces: the errors are bounded by C_r=(g²+g+1)ε∑_{r′≥r}p^(−r′), tending to zero. Trace diagrams modulo p^m are interpreted in the almost category; an integral normalization by p-powers is accompanied by its stated bound.
hypotheses: Normality, generic separability and the boundary ideal being the integral closure of I are hypotheses.
The general trace-integrality/ideal theorem is an extension request to R3, not the finite locally free trace pairing alone.
proofSteps: Invoke trace integrality for the normal generic étale cover and the integrally closed ideal.
Match the actual tower trace with the algebra trace on the interior, then extend bounded sections.
Apply the PSV normalized trace estimate and retain the almost reduction square.

nodes.title: Period lattice transport
nodes.statement: On the Siegel perfectoid tower of genus g, let W be the tautological rank-g flag bundle and ω_Fl=det(W∨). Transport the rational period comparison Lie A⊗O(1)≅π_HT*W to the Hodge line: π_HT*ω_Fl≅ω_A(−g). After choosing a compatible Tate trivialization this identifies the underlying line bundles; its action is transported with the similitude character. On each Lagrangian coordinate chart choose its Plücker frame and compare the finite-level automorphic lattice with the bounded lattice in that frame. Record both inclusions after multiplication by specified p-powers on the quasicompact chart. Hodge-type pullbacks use the actual Hodge Levi torsor comparison and retain the weight-dependent Tate twist. This construction is a transport of supplied bundles, not a second period map.
hypotheses: Use only the 2^g coordinate Lagrangians selecting one of i,g+i, not arbitrary g-element coordinate subsets.
The rational comparison alone gives no equality of integral lattices.
Away-from-p correspondences preserve the transported data; the p-action also moves the flag chart and carries its character.
proofSteps: Import the tautological and Hodge-Levi pullbacks with their Tate twists.
Use finite local frames and quasicompactness to bound the lattice denominators in both directions.
Transport lattice restrictions and tame correspondences through the supplied equivariant isomorphism.

nodes.title: Localized cuspidal sections
nodes.statement: For a nonempty intersection of distinguished opens indexed by J, put s̄_J=∏_{j∈J}s̄_j and r=|J|. On the fixed formal model with ample 𝔏 and boundary ideal 𝔍, the restriction map identifies Γ(D(s̄_J),𝔍/p^m) with colim_k Γ(𝔛,𝔍⊗𝔏^(kr)/p^m), transitions multiplication by s̄_J. The same holds after imposing any positive divisibility condition on k by passing to a cofinal subsequence. The identification carries the actual boundary condition and agrees with bounded chart localization.
hypotheses: The notation on the right means reduction of 𝔍⊗𝔏^(kr).
Use the supplier coherent formal localization theorem over the adhesive valuation base.
proofSteps: Apply the ample distinguished-open localization theorem to the coherent boundary lattice.
Identify its chart sections by TC.0 and TC.1 transport.
Restrict to cofinal k satisfying the desired weight-step congruence.

sources.match: The proof writes sections on a distinguished intersection as the colimit of global twists by powers of its product section; a cofinal weight subsequence gives the same localization.

acceptance: The transition multiplies by the product s̄_J, so the twist increases by |J|.
Do not drop 𝔍 and thereby replace cusp sections with all sections.

nodes.title: Integral cuspidal lifting
nodes.statement: For the projective formal model over O_C, its coherent boundary lattice 𝔍 and ample 𝔏, all sufficiently large t satisfy H¹(𝔛,𝔍⊗𝔏^t)=0. Consequently reduction Γ(𝔛,𝔍⊗𝔏^t)→Γ(𝔛,(𝔍⊗𝔏^t)/p^m) is surjective. Compare these integral sections with classical cuspidal sections on the genuine minimal compactification through the finite genuine-to-image map. This comparison must be proved on the actual ideals, without an assumed global isomorphism of compactifications.
hypotheses: 𝔍 is p-torsion free and coherent by saturation.
O_C is not noetherian; the supplier must furnish the adhesive proper formal Serre theorem and the genuine-to-image cusp-section comparison.
proofSteps: For the coherent p-torsion-free lattice F_t=𝔍⊗𝔏^t on the projective formal model, obtain H¹ vanishing for all large t: either Scholze's route, H¹ of the reduction F_t/p for large t (Serre vanishing for the ample reduction), which gives H¹(F_t/p^j)=0 for every j by the filtration with graded pieces F_t/p, or proper formal Serre vanishing for F_t itself.
Deduce surjectivity of Γ(𝔛,F_t)→Γ(𝔛,F_t/p^m): from integral H¹ vanishing directly, or from H¹(F_t/p^j)=0 for all j together with Γ(𝔛,F_t)=lim_j Γ(𝔛,F_t/p^j) and Mittag-Leffler.
Identify their generic fibres and compare cusp sections through the finite minimal-compactification map.

sources.match: The proof builds the projective formal model with its ample line and boundary lattice, uses ampleness to make H¹ of the twisted boundary lattice modulo p^n vanish for k sufficiently divisible, and concludes that the mod p^n sections are the reductions of the integral ones, whose generic fibre is the space of classical cusp forms.

acceptance: H¹ vanishing of one reduction F_t/p^m alone does not give integral lifting; the deduction needs vanishing for all F_t/p^j (which follows from F_t/p for a p-torsion-free lattice) together with completeness and Mittag-Leffler, or integral H¹ vanishing.
Keep the finite-map cusp-section comparison as an explicit supplier obligation.

nodes.title: Classical section approximation
nodes.statement: At each fixed m and for a finite list of bounded cuspidal sections on chart intersections, there is a common finer finite p-level and sufficiently large twists of the ample automorphic line in any prescribed cofinal positive weight step such that the sections are represented, modulo p^m after the recorded integral losses, by localized reductions of integral classical cusp forms. The representations are compatible with the chosen finite set of tame pullback/trace correspondences. When the classical determinant step is used, choose the weight step a>n in the symplectic case and a≥n in the unitary case.
hypotheses: Use only a finite list at a time, and choose precision to absorb denominators and almost annihilators when passing to almost Čech cohomology.
No uniform single weight or finite p-level for every cohomology class is asserted.
proofSteps: Descend bounded sections and boundary ideals using the ordinary ideal-colimit theorem of TC.2.
Apply localization on the transported approximation atlas and move to a cofinal weight-step sequence.
Use integral cuspidal lifting; repeat at common levels for the finite set of correspondences.

sources.match: The proof first descends finitely many bounded ideal sections modulo the fixed coefficient exponent and then lifts their large twists to genuine finite-level classical cusp sections.

acceptance: Track m, level, twist and boundary ideal in each representative.
This is an approximation of sections, not a lifting of torsion cohomology classes to characteristic zero.

nodes.title: Boundary ideal colimit
nodes.statement: On each standard perfectoid chart and every m≥1, the ordinary module I⁺_∞/p^m is the filtered colimit of the integral boundary ideals modulo p^m at finite image levels, and also of those at genuine minimal levels, with the actual chart restriction maps. This is an ordinary isomorphism. Its proof uses ordinary injectivity on the open interior and approximation plus normalized traces for surjectivity; the trace reduction diagrams used inside the argument remain almost diagrams.
hypotheses: Use the supplied anticanonical good charts, their finite étale interior transitions and actual boundary ideals.
Completion of the ambient plus-ring colimit does not by itself identify its ideal modulo p^m.
proofSteps: Prove injectivity at image levels from the colimit description R⁺/p^m=colim R⁺_(K_p)/p^m of the supplied tower and ϖ-saturation of the ideals (I⁺∩p^mR⁺=p^mI⁺); at genuine levels construct the unique map to I⁺ compatible with evaluation off the boundary and deduce injectivity by valuations.
Approximate a bounded ideal section by finite-level sections; control its boundary values.
Apply boundary-preserving normalized traces with C_r→0 and two successive precision/divisibility corrections, obtaining an ordinary representative modulo p^m.

nodes.title: Perfectoid compact support comparison
nodes.statement: For the Hodge-type tower with tame K^p inside a prime-to-p level-N subgroup, N≥3, C complete algebraically closed over Q_p and m≥1, there is a natural almost isomorphism (colim_Kp H_c^i(X_KpKp,Z/p^m))⊗(O_C/p^m)^a ≅ H^i_top(X̄_∞,(I⁺_∞/p^m)^a). It is realized on the finite Lagrangian rational chart cover by the alternating Čech complex of the actual ideal sections, since all intersections are affinoid perfectoid and almost acyclic. It is compatible with coefficient reductions, p-level pullback and tame Hecke pullback/trace on common refinements.
hypotheses: X̄_∞ is the image compactification, and finite-level X*_K is the genuine proper minimal compactification when applying constructible primitive comparison.
The primitive input must apply to singular proper algebraic compactifications and j!Z/p^m, not only proper smooth spaces.
The left object is CC.8’s fixed-exponent carrier; TC.2 owns this theorem and its geometric vanishing corollaries.
proofSteps: Apply the constructible primitive comparison at each genuine proper finite level; the finite genuine-to-image map is an isomorphism on the interior, so j_! cohomology is the same on both compactifications.
Pass to the filtered p-level system by the étale-cohomology limit theorem for X̄_∞ ~ lim of the finite levels, and identify j!O⁺ with the almost boundary ideal through TC.0.

Compare étale and analytic cohomology of the almost sheaves by étale almost acyclicity on affinoid perfectoid charts; apply almost purity on the interior to compare traces, and almost Čech acyclicity on all intersections to identify the topological complex.

sources.match: Theorem 4.2.1 and its proof compare compact-support completed cohomology with almost integral boundary-ideal cohomology: primitive comparison at finite level, passage to the limit by Corollary 7.18 of Perfectoid spaces, agreement of analytic and étale cohomology (Propositions 6.14 and 7.13 there), the strongly closed boundary sequence, and almost purity for the trace.

nodes.title: Geometric completed amplitude
nodes.statement: If d=dim_C X_K, the fixed-exponent compactly supported completed cohomology colim_Kp H_c^i(X_K,Z/p^m) vanishes for i>d, for every m≥1. Its integral coefficient inverse limit also vanishes there. For m=1 use that the perfectoid image compactification has spectral cohomological dimension ≤d: its underlying space is the inverse limit of the finite-level spaces along spectral maps, each finite level has cohomological dimension ≤d (Huber Proposition 2.5.8, or the limit of all its formal models, each of dimension ≤d), and the bound passes to the limit. Then use faithfulness of tensoring F_p-vector spaces with (O_C/p)^a. Extend to m by Bockstein induction.

proofSteps: Bound the cohomological dimension of each finite-level minimal compactification by d, and pass to the cofiltered spectral limit: every abelian sheaf is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves pulled back from a finite stage.
Apply TC.2 comparison and the faithful F_p coefficient test.
Use Bockstein exact sequences for every exponent, then the defined integral inverse limit.

acceptance: Test all m, not only m=1.

nodes.title: Geometric Iwasawa bounds
nodes.statement: At a torsion-free pro-p level K_p with Λ=Z_p[[K_p]], completed Borel–Moore homology vanishes in degree i>d, its degree-d module is p-torsion free, and for i<d the codimension of completed ordinary homology over Λ is at least d−i. These conclusions specialize CC’s completed duality and grade machinery to the geometric amplitude above. The argument uses the minimum codimension of a violating module and the range l₀=0,q₀=d.

Use the Bockstein argument for top-degree p-torsion freedom.

nodes.title: Classical Hecke topology
nodes.statement: Let T be the abstract tame Hecke algebra Z_p[G(A_f^p)//K^p], with K^p of measure one. For a positive weight step a, give T the weakest topology for which every action map T→End_C(H⁰(X*_K,ω^(ak)⊗I)) is continuous, over all sufficiently small p-levels K_p (K=K_pK^p) and all k≥1; here H⁰(X*_K,ω^(ak)⊗I) is the finite-dimensional C-vector space of classical cusp forms on the genuine minimal compactification and End_C carries its p-adic topology. Denote this topological algebra T_cl. Let T_(K,k) be the image of T in that endomorphism ring. Because pullback and the integral trace preserve the integral cusp sections, T_(K,k) is a finitely generated torsion-free Z_p-module, and its subspace topology is its p-adic topology. Hence finite intersections of the ideals ker(T→T_(K,k)/p^r) form a basis of open ideals. T_cl can be nonseparated; passing to its separated completion is a separate operation. The weight step used for determinant interpolation satisfies a>n for Sp and a≥n for U.
hypotheses: Fix the tame level and the same abstract Hecke generators as in TC.3; the classical spaces are taken for every weight ak with k≥1, not only for large k.

The defining spaces are the rational cusp-form spaces with their p-adic topology. An integral lattice is a way of describing the neighbourhoods, valid only for a Hecke-stable lattice; it is not an extra datum of the definition.
proofSteps: Use the classical Hecke action on each finite-dimensional cusp space and form the initial topology, keeping its possible closure of zero.

Pullback and the integral boundary-ideal trace of Lemma 4.3.2 preserve the integral cusp sections, so each T_(K,k) preserves a bounded lattice and is a finitely generated Z_p-module; a lattice in a finite-dimensional Q_p-subspace of the Banach space End_C carries the p-adic topology.
Describe the basic neighbourhoods as finite intersections of ker(T→T_(K,k)/p^r), equivalently of the kernels of T→End(Λ/p^rΛ) for Hecke-stable lattices Λ.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.3.1 and footnote 18, p. 1025; Corollaries 5.1.7 and 5.1.11, pp. 1036 and 1038

Corollary 5.1.7 shows the image of T there is flat over Z_p with finite étale generic fibre, and the proof of Corollary 5.1.11 uses that every open ideal of T_cl contains a finite intersection of the ideals ker(T_cl→T_K,k), together with the weight progression, which needs the discrete-series range of Proposition 5.1.1.

The E₂ rows have tower cohomological degree 0≤j≤d, so each finite-level target has a filtration of length at most d+1. Define the finite-level action on this supplied complex before invoking IHG ghost/filtered-action nilpotence. Coefficient inverse limits are taken after p-level colimits. This is ordinary polynomial substitution using the existing composition ring homomorphism. It records the opposite character weights used to separate the Levi factor; it creates no new polynomial carrier.

nodes.title: Twisted product separation
nodes.statement: Let R be any commutative ring, n≥0, u∈Rˣ and P,Q,P′,Q′∈R[X] have degree at most n and constant term 1. If PQ=P′Q′, P(X/u)Q(uX)=P′(X/u)Q′(uX), and 1−u^(2j) is a unit for 1≤j≤n, then P=P′ and Q=Q′. Coefficientwise induction solves the two equations at order j by a unit determinant. This works over nonreduced rings and commutes with ring base change preserving the unit hypotheses.
hypotheses: For n=0 all four polynomials equal 1.
The condition is invertibility of each difference, not merely inequality of u^(2j) and 1.
proofSteps: At the first differing coefficient j, the untwisted equation gives δP_j+δQ_j=0.
The twisted equation gives u^(−j)δP_j+u^jδQ_j=0; eliminate using the unit 1−u^(2j).
Induct to n; coefficients above n vanish.

nodes.title: Weight factorization uniqueness
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring S and a finite subset M⊂Z, a formal series Q(T,X)∈S[T,T⁻¹][[X]], Q≡1 mod X, has at most one expression ∏_{m∈M}Q_m(T^mX) with Q_m∈1+XS[[X]]. If Q is polynomial in X and such a factorization exists, every Q_m is polynomial. The assertion is natural for S→S′. Finite weight support is essential.
hypotheses: Only finitely many nonconstant factors are allowed.
The source’s leading-order and polynomiality arguments are used in their corrected forms recorded in sourceIssues.

For polynomiality shift all weights to nonnegative values and isolate the least weight.
Reexpand in T with coefficients polynomial in X; induction removes the least-weight factor and continues over the finite set.

nodes.title: Weighted determinant unit law
nodes.statement: Suppose a group-indexed family of polynomials P_g^(m), constant term 1, degree at most n_m and finite weight support, is realized by an h-dimensional determinant D̃:R[G][V,V⁻¹]→R[T,T⁻¹], h=∑n_m, with D̃(1−XV^kg)=∏_m P_g^(m)(T^(km)X). For each R-algebra S construct the multiplicative natural unit law D₀^(m):1+US[G][[U]]→1+US[[U]] by finite-weight factorization of D̃, with D₀^(m)(1−U^a xg)=P_g^(m)(U^a x), a≥1. Polynomial inputs have polynomial outputs. The natural algebra law is obtained by evaluating D₀^(m)(1+U(x−1)) at U=1.
hypotheses: G is any group; each group-algebra expression has finite support. Continuity at later profinite finite-image limits is supplied separately.
The characteristic identities hold for every g and every integer k, not only Frobenius or k=1.

Separate finitely many weights using the preceding series uniqueness theorem.
Prove evaluation multiplicativity through the nilpotent kernel argument, using the correct noncommutative inverse order.

It is compatible with every ring base change and with nilpotent quotients. It is obtained as an actual natural homogeneous multiplicative polynomial law, not by pointwise selection of polynomial roots. The degrees are forced by the unit leading coefficient of the full characteristic polynomial and h=∑n_m, combined with the supplier’s direct-factor decomposition of a multiplicative polynomial law into homogeneous degrees.

Then J^N=0 and I′⊂J·R[T,T⁻¹]. Hence any characteristic constraints realized over R[T,T⁻¹]/I′ descend to (R/J)[T,T⁻¹] with the same nilpotence exponent. nodes.title: Boundary Satake polynomials
nodes.statement: At v∉S let e_i be the elementary symmetric normalized GL_n Satake generators, e₀=1 and e_n a unit; q=q_v. Define P_v(X)=∑_{i=0}^n(−1)^i q^(i(n+1)/2)e_iX^i and Q_v(X)=∑_{i=0}^n(−1)^i q^(−i(n+1)/2)(e_{n−i}/e_n)X^i. Q is the constant-one dual polynomial, equivalently the normalized reciprocal of P. Under the unnormalized Siegel-Levi Satake map the ambient polynomial is (1−X)P_v(X)Q_v(X) for Sp_2n, and P_v(X)Q_vc(q_vX) for U(n,n), both at split and inert places (v^c=v in the inert case, q_v=q_v⁺²). For the standard double-coset generators U_i, e_i=q^(−i(n−i)/2)U_i; hence P_v(X)=P_standard^rec(q_vX), where P_standard is IHG.3’s monic polynomial. Square roots used to describe Satake parameters disappear in the integral coefficients.

General real fields require the precise Arthur input; general CM fields require Mok. The unconditional CM branch requires F to contain an imaginary quadratic field, S to be pulled back from rational primes including p and all F/Q ramification, and uses unitary similitude Shimura varieties with Shin’s cohomological base change.

The actual Borel–Serre stratum is a unipotent nilmanifold bundle over X_KM; in this Siegel case U is commutative and its fibre is a torus. The ALS boundary triangle, projection and zero section show that the ambient boundary Hecke annihilator is contained in the annihilator of H!^i(X_KM,O/p^m), with action through the unnormalized Satake map. Apply the preceding ambient polynomial identity. This is a kernel containment and resulting quotient, not a direct-summand assertion for full boundary cohomology.

nodes.title: Ambient interior error bound
nodes.statement: Let A₀ be the finite Hecke image on H!^i(X_KM,O/p^m) in the Siegel-Levi specialization. With d=[F:Q]n(n+1)/2 in the real case and d=[F⁺:Q]n² in the CM case, there is I⊂A₀ with I^(2(d+1))=0 and a continuous ambient determinant of rank h over A₀/I with characteristic polynomial (1−X)P_vQ_v or P_vQ_vc(q_vX). The nilpotence is obtained by combining the length d+1 fixed-exponent descent filtration with the two boundary/interior steps, using IHG’s imported filtered-module error algebra.

The perfectoid inputs need tame level inside a level-N subgroup, N≥3 prime to p. Reach it by adjoining the places over an auxiliary prime ℓ≥3, ℓ≠p, to S⁺ without changing K; the result for S⁺∪{ℓ} is then returned to S by stabilizing over infinitely many ℓ, so that the exponent d+1 per filtration is not lost.

The ambient Hecke image A on H_c^i(X_K,Z/p^m) is finite and contains A_ℓ, so infinitely many ℓ give the same extended ideal J=J_ℓA. For two such ℓ₁≠ℓ₂ both determinants live over A/J and agree at Frobenius outside S∪{ℓ₁,ℓ₂}; by density they are equal, hence unramified at ℓ₁ and ℓ₂, and give a determinant of G_F,S over A/J with the prescribed characteristic polynomials at every v∉S.

nodes.title: Auxiliary character realization
nodes.statement: For a finite-order character χ:G_F,S′→W(F̄_p)ˣ of order prime to p, realize its class-field character as a degree-zero cohomology class at a refined GL_n level. Its χ-isotypic projector is integral, since the covering index is prime to p, and cup product gives the split injection of the original interior module into the χ-twisted interior module. The Levi polynomial changes to P_v(X/χ(Frob_v)), and its dual to Q_v(χ(Frob_v)X); in the CM term use the conjugate character at v^c. Ramification is included in S′, and later auxiliary-prime descent restores S. This produces actual input determinants at the twisted level, not formal twists of unsupported eigenvalues.

Choose the refinement realizing the finite class-field character and keep all coefficient extensions.

Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory normalizes every Artin map by arithmetic Frobenius. nodes.title: Cyclotomic factor continuation
nodes.statement: Choose a finite extension L₀ containing F, Galois over F⁺, trivializing the residual root data and, in the CM case, the residual cyclotomic character. For an auxiliary odd ℓ≠p, let F_ℓ^cycl/F be the cyclotomic Z_ℓ-extension and S_ℓ=S∪{v|ℓ}; use the maximal pro-p extension of L₀F_ℓ^cycl unramified outside S_ℓ. On the finite Artinian coefficient factors, the requested residual-kernel theorem factors each ambient determinant through the quotient retaining this pro-p kernel and the finite residual image. Odd prime-to-p characters of arbitrarily large ℓ-power order separate an element outside the cyclotomic kernel: choose χ with χ(g)^(2j)≠1 for 1≤j≤n; then χ(g)^(2j) is a root of unity of ℓ-power order different from 1, and since ℓ≠p, 1−χ(g)^(2j) is a unit of W(F̄_p). Twisted-product separation determines the continuous Levi coefficients there. Stabilize a common error ideal I₀ across infinitely many characters and auxiliary primes using finiteness of the coefficient Hecke image. Two distinct primes, chosen away from the finite extension degree, cover the omitted kernels and descend the coefficient functions to G_F,S, removing the extra ramification. The coefficients are independent of auxiliary choices, with I₀^(4(d+1))=0.

Work first after the finite coefficient extension needed for the character values. Comparing each character uses the sum ideal Ĩ_χ=I₁+I_χ. Algebraic characteristic-coefficient subring descent on G×Z, via Amitsur’s formula, constructs the natural law over the Laurent coefficient subring; the Laurent ring is not assumed compact. Apply every T↦T^a substitution and the coefficient-ideal theorem to replace the error by an ideal generated by coefficients with exponent 4(d+1), then contract to the original finite Hecke image A₀ and descend using its characteristic coefficients. In the real case retain the factor (1−X) as weight zero in the full determinant; the weight −1 factor is extracted only in levi-interior-determinant. Weights −1,+1 carry P_g and its dual, with the CM conjugate/cyclotomic factor retained.

nodes.statement: For GL_n/F with F totally real or CM, S conjugation-stable containing p and all places ramified over F⁺, and K hyperspecial outside S, realize the Borel–Serre boundary with finite coefficients O/ϖ^m by its actual finite stratification and nilmanifold-fibre complexes. Its Hecke-module cohomology has a filtration of length bounded only by [F:Q] and n whose graded terms are subquotients of finite sums of lower-rank Levi cohomology/group-cohomology terms, with action through the full unnormalized Satake transform and the actual coefficient twists. Combining lower-rank determinants with those twists gives a degree-n boundary determinant modulo an ideal of uniformly bounded nilpotence. Stacky levels and arbitrary finite-free algebraic lattices are handled by finite-level coefficient trivialization and Hochschild–Serre descent, using the bounded geometric row range rather than the unbounded group-cohomology direction.

nodes.title: Finite torsion determinant assembly
nodes.statement: Specialize the infrastructure to Scholze’s GL_n arithmetic output: there exists N=N([F:Q],n) such that for every K=K_SK^S⊂∏GL_n(O_Fv), every finite-free Z_p algebraic representation lattice M_ξ, all i≥0 and m≥1, the finite Hecke image A(K,ξ,i,m)=im(T_F,S→End(H^i(X_K,M_ξ/p^m))) admits I with I^N=0 and a continuous degree-n determinant over A/I with D(1−XFrob_v)=P_v(X) for v∉S. Use the source’s stack interpretation at nonneat levels. The theorem is an assembly on this actual family, with the classical input branch and field/S restrictions explicitly inherited from TC.3. It supplies no all-reductive-group theorem and no explicit value of N beyond the proven interior bound.

Unconditional CM: imaginary quadratic subfield and S pulled back from S_Q containing p and F/Q ramification; otherwise the matching Arthur/Mok input is a hypothesis.
proofSteps: For neat level and trivial coefficients put B_i=im(H^i→H^i_∂). The exact sequence is 0→H!^i→H^i→B_i→0. Let A! and A_B be the faithful Hecke images on these two factors; A_B is a quotient of the full boundary Hecke image. Thus the map A→A!×A_B is well defined.

An operator in this map’s kernel kills H!^i and sends H^i into H!^i, so the kernel has square zero. First push the boundary determinant along its quotient map to A_B and glue on the joint product image; pulling the error back multiplies its exponent by at most two.

Use characteristic-compatible determinant descent on the joint quotient. Choose a neat normal K′⊂K on which M_ξ/p^m is trivial and descend by the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre sequence H^a(K/K′,H^b(X_K′,M_ξ/p^m))⇒H^(a+b)(X_K,M_ξ/p^m): its rows vanish above the dimension of the manifold X_K′, so every degree has a filtration of uniformly bounded length although the group cohomology of K/K′ is unbounded.

nodes.title: Integral coefficient transport
nodes.statement: For fixed K,ξ,i let A_m be the finite Hecke image on H^i(X_K,M_ξ/p^m), H=H^i(X_K,M_ξ) the finite Z_p-module, and B the closed simultaneous image of T_F,S in ∏_{m≥1}A_m. The UCT injection H/p^m↪H^i(X_K,M_ξ/p^m) makes each action on H/p^m continuous for the B-topology and compatible in m. Taking their inverse limit extends the integral action to B. The integral Hecke image A_Zp⊂End_Zp(H) is a finite Z_p-submodule, hence compact and closed, so density gives a surjection B→A_Zp. Choose any finite-exponent error ideals I_m with their common bound N and set J=B∩∏I_m. The injective simultaneous projections give J^N=0. The compact ring B/J embeds in ∏A_m/I_m and contains the common Hecke coefficients; IHG compact coefficient gluing constructs its continuous degree-n determinant. Push it along B/J→A_Zp/image(J); the uniform exponent N is unchanged. Varying levels uses closed joint action rings and common quotients; individual canonical maps A_m→A_r are not required.
hypotheses: Use products, not direct sums, for simultaneous coefficient exponents.
Integral cohomology H is a finite Z_p-module; UCT includes the next-degree Tor term.

The integral image is closed in End_Zp(H); density of the original Hecke image and compactness of B make its extended image exactly A_Zp, not just a dense subring.

Bound J by the existing arbitrary-family nilpotence theorem, embed B/J into the product of finite coefficient quotients, apply compact determinant gluing using their common characteristic coefficients, and push the law and ideal to A_Zp.

nodes.title: Four route Hecke compatibility
nodes.statement: For the finite Hecke image on an interior GL_n module H!^i(X_K,O/p^m) realized by the Siegel boundary diagram, use the actual common refinements and joint action rings. After its quantified quotient A→A/I with I^(4(d+1))=0, four action/characteristic calculations agree: (1) the ambient Shimura finite-level support diagram, fixed-exponent completion and almost boundary-ideal Čech comparison followed by classical section approximation; (2) the ambient boundary action on the GL_n interior image through unnormalized Levi Satake; (3) auxiliary-character Laurent realization and degree-n determinant extraction; (4) the integral GL_n spherical polynomial from IHG.3 after reciprocal/geometric-Frobenius and ε⁻¹ transport. The common value at every v∉S is P_v in (A/I)[X]. For a full ordinary GL_n finite-level module with coefficients M_ξ/p^m, apply these squares to its interior and lower-rank boundary subquotients, then glue by TC.4 boundary induction and the assembly quotient I^N=0, N=N([F:Q],n). The squares commute under ring base change and coefficient/level pullback/trace on joint quotients. Almost errors in route (1) are discharged by finite-coefficient faithfulness; the nilpotent ideal is a separate error.
hypotheses: These are maps of actions and characteristic coefficients, not a purported canonical map taking an arbitrary cohomology class to a polynomial.
Agreement under a coefficient or level change is stated only after the named common quotient maps, not by inventing A_m→A_r.

The perfectoid comparison is on the ambient Hodge-type Shimura tower. There is no asserted perfectoid compactification or direct class-to-section map for an arbitrary GL_n locally symmetric space. Compose boundary Satake and character-twist identities with the extracted determinant characteristic formula.
Use determinant uniqueness on dense Frobenius data and the IHG base-change maps to identify the two composites on each common coefficient quotient.

For ordinary coefficients descend and filter through the interior and smaller-Levi boundary modules; compare each graded action square and use the uniform assembly ideal I^N=0 rather than asserting a perfectoid map on GL_n classes.

nodes.title: Residual and local specialization
nodes.statement: A finite-field Hecke eigensystem on the finite torsion module kills the nilpotent ideal, so IHG reconstruction gives a continuous semisimple degree-n representation over an algebraic closure with characteristic P_v, unique up to conjugacy. For a split absolutely irreducible residual system over a finite field k, localize and complete a Hecke coefficient ring on which that system occurs: a finite torsion action ring, or the integral action ring when the eigensystem is in its support. After the coefficient extension needed to identify k and its residual basis, the determinant lives over the resulting complete henselian local ring Â/Î, with Î^N=0. IHG irreducible reconstruction gives a representation over Â/Î with its local Hecke coefficient map. Uniqueness after fixing the residual basis is up to strict conjugacy. This asserts neither a lift to Â nor an integral action localization at an eigensystem appearing only through torsion in the next cohomology group; such systems use the closed simultaneous torsion action ring.

Choose a supported local action ring and apply completion/coefficient change to its determinant and error ideal; record Î^N=0 and the identified residual representation.

For each finite coefficient quotient, continuity of the determinant gives an open normal group kernel; its full-matrix Cayley–Hamilton realization factors through the same finite quotient. Hence the reconstructed matrices are continuous in the inverse-limit coefficient topology. Compare by strict conjugacy after fixing the residual basis; no lifting through Î is asserted.
